title: Add more useful items to "More Actions" context menu of application in Task Manager
line: The task manager's More menu now has Configure Special Window Settings and Configure Special Application Settings, like KWin's window menu.
explanation: The task context menu's More submenu only mirrored the basic window operations; KWin's window-rules entries were only reachable from the titlebar menu or Alt+F3, so windows without a titlebar had no mouse path to them. The change adds "Configure Special Window Settings…" and "Configure Special Application Settings…" to the More submenu for single windows on Wayland. They launch the window rules KCM with the window's uuid (plus whole-app), exactly the command KWin's own menu runs, so the editor opens pre-filled for that window or application.

commits.message:
applets/taskmanager: add special window settings to More menu

Windows without a titlebar offered no way to reach KWin's window rules
for them, as the task's More menu lacked the entries from KWin's menu.
Add them there, opening the window rules editor for that window or app.

BUG: 458527

patches.diff:
From 38f39544feaff9511c2ed7e0ffb75bcfb4a8d459 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: =?UTF-8?q?Niccol=C3=B2=20Venerandi?= <niccolo@venerandi.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 23:29:49 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] applets/taskmanager: add special window settings to More menu

Windows without a titlebar offered no way to reach KWin's window rules
for them, as the task's More menu lacked the entries from KWin's menu.
Add them there, opening the window rules editor for that window or app.

BUG: 458527
---
 applets/taskmanager/qml/ContextMenu.qml | 26 +++++++++++++++++++++++++
 1 file changed, 26 insertions(+)

diff --git a/applets/taskmanager/qml/ContextMenu.qml b/applets/taskmanager/qml/ContextMenu.qml
index fe837049fc..b34cdf21a6 100644
--- a/applets/taskmanager/qml/ContextMenu.qml
+++ b/applets/taskmanager/qml/ContextMenu.qml
@@ -12,6 +12,7 @@ import org.kde.plasma.plasmoid
 import org.kde.plasma.core as PlasmaCore
 import org.kde.plasma.extras as PlasmaExtras
 
+import org.kde.kcmutils as KCMUtils
 import org.kde.taskmanager as TaskManager
 import org.kde.plasma.private.mpris as Mpris
 import plasma.applet.org.kde.plasma.taskmanager as TaskManagerApplet
@@ -802,6 +803,31 @@ PlasmaExtras.Menu {
                 onClicked: tasksModel.requestToggleExcludeFromCapture(menu.modelIndex)
             }
 
+            PlasmaExtras.MenuItem {
+                visible: windowRulesItem.visible
+                separator: true
+            }
+
+            PlasmaExtras.MenuItem {
+                id: windowRulesItem
+
+                visible: Qt.platform.pluginName === "wayland" && menu.visualParent && menu.get(TaskManager.AbstractTasksModel.IsWindow) && !menu.get(TaskManager.AbstractTasksModel.IsGroupParent)
+
+                text: i18nc("@action:inmenu", "Configure Special &Window Settings…")
+                icon: "preferences-system-windows-actions"
+
+                onClicked: KCMUtils.KCMLauncher.open(["kcm_kwinrules", "--args", "uuid=" + menu.get(TaskManager.AbstractTasksModel.WinIdList)[0]])
+            }
+
+            PlasmaExtras.MenuItem {
+                visible: windowRulesItem.visible
+
+                text: i18nc("@action:inmenu", "Configure S&pecial Application Settings…")
+                icon: "preferences-system-windows-actions"
+
+                onClicked: KCMUtils.KCMLauncher.open(["kcm_kwinrules", "--args", "uuid=" + menu.get(TaskManager.AbstractTasksModel.WinIdList)[0] + " whole-app"])
+            }
+
             PlasmaExtras.MenuItem {
                 separator: true
             }
--

More submenu with the two new entries
Master: the task menu offers no way to open window rules for Konsole
Configure Special Application Settings… opens the rules editor pre-filled for Konsole

reviews.text: Clean, minimal addition to the Task Manager's More submenu that exposes KWin's 'Configure Special Window Settings…' and 'Configure Special Application Settings…' actions for single windows on Wayland, using KWin's wording, icon, and kcmshell6 kcm_kwinrules arguments via KCMUtils.KCMLauncher. Mnemonics do not collide, separators hide cleanly for grouped tasks, and the screenshots demonstrate both the submenu and the pre-filled Window Rules dialog. Omitting KWin's internal 'Set Window Shortcut…' dialog is reasonable since persistent window shortcuts are directly available in the Window Rules editor.
